## 2

I understand why some space images can seem difficult to trust—photos can be edited, and institutions can make mistakes. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on photographs alone. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s curved shadow appears during lunar eclipses, and satellites, GPS, circumnavigation, and time zones all work because Earth is roughly spherical. These observations come from many independent people and systems, so rejecting every photograph would not explain the much broader body of evidence.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. The shorter blue and violet waves get scattered in all directions more strongly than the longer red and orange waves. We see the scattered light coming from across the sky, so the sky looks blue. Violet is scattered even more than blue, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more reds and oranges.

## 4

雨落在夜色里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕成一团昏黄的光，路面映着车灯，仿佛铺满了摇晃的星星。远处偶尔传来汽车驶过积水的声响，随后又归于安静。屋檐下的风带着潮湿的泥土味，树叶在雨中低低地颤动。有人撑伞匆匆走过，脚步声渐渐远去。此刻，城市像暂时卸下了白日的喧闹，只剩雨声陪着孤独而温柔的夜。
